newsitem.title: USA: Spy case will not hinder U.S-Korea alliance - Perry.
newsitem.headline: Spy case will not hinder U.S-Korea alliance - Perry.

text.p: The arrest of a U.S. Navy intelligence employee on charges of spying for South Korea will not hinder close military ties between the two countries, U.S. Defence Secretary William Perry said on Sunday.

"We have a compelling reason for maintaining a strong military alliance with South Korea. We are both profoundly affected by the threat from North Korea. That theat still is very much on our minds," he told reporters flying home with him from a visit to Nordic countries.

Perry declined for legal reasons to comment directly on details of the arrest in Washington Tuesday of Robert Kim, 56, an 18-year government employee who worked at a U.S. Navy intelligence office in Suitland, Maryland. But asked if it would damage ties with Seoul, he said without hesitation:

"To directly answer your question, both the Republic of South Korea and the United States believe that the military alliance between our two countries is of vital importance to our countries and we will maintain and, if anything, strengthen that military alliance."

Kim, arrested at a diplomatic reception at Fort Myer, Virginia, was charged with passing classified information to a naval attache at the South Korean Embassy in Washington identified as Capt. Dong-Il Baek.

He suggested that the Kim incident was far outweighed by mutual worries about North Korea, mentioning the recent grounding of a North Korean submarine off South Korea and subsequent killing of a number of men from that submarine by military forces in the South.
